name: genealogy-mcp
description: Find your family history with Claude: 171 archives and databases, name variants, old calendars, kinship, DNA, evidence checks, a research project that remembers, edits to your own GEDCOM tree.
long_description:
Turns Claude into a careful genealogist.

- **Where to look:** 124 archives and databases for Russia and the former USSR, Ukraine, Belarus, Poland, the Baltics, the Caucasus and Central Asia, Germany, Western and Northern Europe, the British Isles, the Americas, Australia and New Zealand; which archive holds the records of a historical province today, whose land it was in a given year (Bessarabia), and which church kept a village's books.
- **How to search:** name variants, pre-1918 spelling, male and female surname forms, 9 transliterations, Daitch–Mokotoff codes, Moldovan surnames in Romanian and Russian forms; live search in the Internet Archive full text, WikiTree, Open Archives and Wikidata.
- **Record guides** in English, Russian and Ukrainian (the main ones also in Spanish, Portuguese, Polish and German).
- **Dates:** Julian ↔ Gregorian, church feasts, the Hebrew and French Republican calendars, Church Slavonic numerals, birth years from ages or estimated from relatives.
- **Is it our person?** Evidence checks, parent hypotheses from patronymics, kinship names in Russian, English and Romanian, DNA (shared cM).
- **A project that remembers:** people, sources with full citations, a search log with negative results, what has already been read in which films, GEDCOM import and export — kept in a folder on your computer.
- **Your own tree:** give Claude the path of the .ged file from MyHeritage, Ancestry, Gramps or RootsMagic — it reads, searches and changes it in place, rewriting only the changed lines, showing them first and keeping a copy.

Nothing is sent anywhere except the query of an online search you ask for, to that one site.

projects_folder.title: Research projects folder
projects_folder.description: Where the research projects (people, sources, search log) are kept between conversations.

site_folder.title: Family archive site (gene-archive), optional
site_folder.description: The folder of your gene-archive site (needs gene-archive installed) — or put the path of your .ged tree file in your request.

tools.name: find_sources
tools.description: Find genealogy databases and archives for a country (or region), period and kind of records — 171 sources across Russia and the former USSR, the Caucasus and Central Asia, Eastern, Western and Northern Europe, Germany, the British Isles, the Americas, Australia and New Zealand, each with what it holds and how to search it well.

tools.name: source_details
tools.description: Everything about one source from the catalogue (by id from find_sources): coverage, access, search tips.

tools.name: search_links
tools.description: Ready search links (open them in a browser) in the sources that take a search URL — FamilySearch, Internet Archive full text, Find a Grave, Arolsen, Geneteka, Open List and others — for a name, with the name's variants.

tools.name: where_are_records
tools.description: Which archives now hold the records (parish registers, revision lists, confession lists, civil records) of a province of the Russian Empire, the Kingdom of Poland, Galicia, Bukovina, East Prussia, the Baltics or the Caucasus — borders moved, so this is often not the archive of today's region.

tools.name: search_online
tools.description: Search an open database live and get the matching records back (title, date, place, link, snippet).

tools.name: place_history
tools.description: Look a place up in Wikidata: what administrative units it was part of (with years where known), coordinates and the Wikipedia article — a first step to the uezd, province and parish of a village — and the church its books were kept in, where that attachment is known.

tools.name: plan_research
tools.description: A step-by-step research plan for a country and period: which records exist, which guides to read and which sources to search, in order (free and country-specific first).

tools.name: film_reading_plan
tools.description: A plan for reading unindexed FamilySearch films page by page for a parish, years and parts: which films to read in which order, thumbnails to find the book (title pages, end-of-year summaries naming the church) and full frames only for the record pages, a rough request budget split into sessions under the site's variable rate limit (pause at least an hour after HTTP 429, no parallel sessions), and what to log with project_coverage.

tools.name: name_variants
tools.description: All the forms a name can take in records (and its Daitch–Mokotoff Soundex codes): spelling variants, pre-1918 orthography, male/female surname forms (Колодин/Колодина, Kowalski/Kowalska, Kazlauskas/Kazlauskienė), transliterations (passport, BGN, German, French, Polish, Romanian, Spanish, Ukrainian, scholarly) and given-name equivalents across languages (Иван = Іоаннъ = Jan = Johann = Juan).

tools.name: normalize_date
tools.description: A date as people write it ('около 1899', 'between 1900 and 1905', '9 de octubre de 1899', '9.10.1899') → ISO or GEDCOM ('ABT 1899', 'BET 1900 AND 1905', '9 OCT 1899', '1899-10-09').

tools.name: convert_calendar
tools.description: Convert between calendars of old records: Julian (old style; Russia until February 1918: +10 days in the 1600s, +11 in the 1700s, +12 in the 1800s, +13 in 1900–1918), Gregorian, Hebrew (Jewish registers, tombstones) and the French Republican calendar (1792–1805).

tools.name: feast_date
tools.description: The date of a church feast or fast in a given year (Julian and Gregorian), including movable feasts counted from Easter.

tools.name: cyrillic_numerals
tools.description: Church Slavonic numerals in old registers and church books: ҂аѡ҃п = 1880, ѳі = 19 (11–19 are written units first).

tools.name: dna_match
tools.description: Which relationships a DNA match fits, from the amount of shared DNA (Shared cM Project 4.0 ranges), closest first.

tools.name: birth_year_from_age
tools.description: The birth-year range implied by an age in a record (census, confession list, death record), exact and loose.

tools.name: estimate_birth_year
tools.description: A birth year estimated from relatives (eldest child −27, spouse and siblings ±8, parents +18…+45, first marriage at about 22) and ages in records: a GEDCOM date (BET … AND … or ABT …), the most likely year and a ready explanation to save with it.

tools.name: kinship
tools.description: What B is to A, named in Russian, English and Romanian (троюродный брат / second cousin / văr de gradul 2, двоюродный дед / great-uncle), with the expected share of DNA.

tools.name: check_match
tools.description: Is the person in a found record ours? Compares fact by fact (with name variants and Julian/rounded-age tolerance) and gives a verdict: confirmed (2+ independent facts beyond the name), probable, insufficient, conflict or different_person.

tools.name: parent_hypothesis
tools.description: A working hypothesis about a parent from a patronymic: the father's given name it implies (Петрович → Пётр, Ильич → Илья), each candidate ranked by name, surname, village and age with the arguments for and against (a grandson named after him, godparents and sureties of his surname, his household listing a child of this name), a warning for a namesake from another village, and the record that would settle it.

tools.name: audit_tree
tools.description: Audit a family tree from any program (GEDCOM) for impossible facts (born after the mother's death, a parent under 14, death before birth), possible duplicates and gaps (no sources, no dates, people cut off from the tree) — a to-do list for the next search.

tools.name: draft_archive_request
tools.description: A draft letter to a registry office or an archive (Russian ZAGS, state, military and FSB archives; any archive in English, Spanish or Portuguese), with what to attach.

tools.name: record_guide
tools.description: How to read and find a kind of record: parish registers, confession lists, revision lists, household books, WWI and WWII records, repression files, passenger lists, censuses, European civil registration, Latin America, evaluating evidence — in English, Russian, Ukrainian, and partly Spanish, Portuguese, Polish, German.

tools.name: glossary
tools.description: Old Russian terms from records — estates, kinship by marriage (шурин, деверь, золовка), archive citation (фонд, опись, дело, лист), administrative units, pre-1918 letters — explained.

tools.name: project_view
tools.description: Read the research project kept between conversations — or a family's gene-archive site folder, or the user's own tree in a GEDCOM file: summary (people, open leads, recent searches, problems), one record with its family and sources, a text search, the full search log, or the tree checks.

tools.name: project_save
tools.description: Add or change a person, family, source or research lead in the project.

tools.name: project_policy
tools.description: Configure this project's policy only (dry_run by default; save within the owner's authorization).

tools.name: project_log
tools.description: Write a line in the project's research log, so nobody searches the same place twice.

tools.name: project_coverage
tools.description: What has already been read in the registers: parish → year → part → film and frames → status (complete, partial up to No.

tools.name: project_transfer
tools.description: Export the project as GEDCOM 5.5.1 (for MyHeritage, Ancestry, Gramps, Geni…) next to the project file, or start a new project from a GEDCOM exported by another program.
